title: Legacy Model Lifecycle Management
business: Enterprise teams maintaining legacy API integrations
problem: Applications relying on retired models like Claude Instant 1.1 experience service failures because requests to retired models will fail.
solution: The solution involves auditing current API usage via the Claude Console to identify retired model dependencies and migrating those workloads to active, supported models.
steps: Access the Usage page in the Claude Console to retrieve an audit of API activity.
Export the usage data to a CSV file to identify specific API keys and model identifiers.
Cross-reference the identified models against the official documentation to confirm retirement status.
Update application code to point to a recommended active model replacement.
Perform thorough testing with the new model to ensure output consistency before the retirement deadline.
outcome: Restored service reliability and compliance with current model support standards.
limitation: The primary tradeoff is the potential for performance variance when switching models; developers must verify behavior through testing, as newer models may interpret prompts differently than the legacy version.
